dialog.text: Why do you hang out with that guy? I find him super annoying.

dialog.speaker: B
dialog.text: He's actually not too bad in small doses but he's not really a close friend. He's my buddy's girlfriend's boyfriend so it's not really my place to tell him he can't come to parties or whatever.

dialog.speaker: A
dialog.text: I'd keep him at an arm's length for sure. I'm not sure what it is but there is something about him that I don't really trust.

dialog.speaker: B
dialog.text: I've got the same feeling and I certainly don't intend to have him become part of our core circle of friends. I don't really care if he stays on the fringes though. He might not be that bad. He just seems a bit socially awkward and a bit of an oddball.

vocabulary.definition: This is very common in spoken English. If you like a person "in small doses" it means you like to see them but not too often. If you see them too much you might get sick of them, but once in a while is pretty fun.
If something isn't really "your place to do something" it means that it's not really your business or you don't really have the social right to do something, even if you want to.

vocabulary.term: I'd keep him at an arm's length for sure
vocabulary.definition: If you "keep someone at arm's length" it means that you are keeping some distance from them. You don't let the person know too much about your personal life and you don't let them get too close to you.

This means that there is some feeling you get from a person, but you don't really know the exact reason why. There is something about her that everyone likes. I'm not really sure what it is but everyone she meets has only nice things to say about her.

Someone's "core circle of friends" is their group of their closest friends. If you go to a party of 50 people, you may have your best and closest friends there, (your core group) and a bunch of new people you don't know too well. You may have met these other people before but certainly wouldn't consider them your "best friends". They may be (friends of friends)
If someone in a group of friends stays on the "fringes" it means that they never get too close personally with the main group of people.

If someone is "socially awkward" it means they are just kind of weird in groups of people and everyone can notice that there is something a bit weird about them when they meet new people. They might be really great people, but they don't make good first impressions.
